newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rates talk supports stronger Australia bonds.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rates talk supports stronger Australia bonds.

text.p: *Australian bonds finish firmer on renewed rate cut hopes after Wednesday's CPI data confirmed low inflation status.
*Curve continues its recent steepening trend as short end benefits most from rate cut speculation.
Australian bonds recovered from Wednesday's weakening to rise strongly on Thursday as renewed expectations of a rate cut supported the market.
Bonds were given a good start by a firming U.S. Treasuries market and pushed ahead from the open on hopes of an easing.

While a bullish market had sold off on Wednesday after the CPI only met rather than exceeded expectations, the confirmation of low inflation was seen as giving the Reserve Bank room to cut if it felt the economy needed a further boost. Bonds rallied ahead of 9.30 a.m., the usual time for rate announcements, but they pulled back slightly when no change was made.
The pull back was most notable at the short end, but bonds remained well supported, and, aided by a continuing firmer tone in Treasuries, rose in the afternoon to finish near their highs.
The market is expected to remain supported by expectations of a cut, with events over the next week or so seen playing an important role in determining sentiment.
Markets are expected to remain on edge about the chances of a cut over next the next week or so.
"The next 10 days sees a bucketload of potential dynamite for the markets," Citibank Australia chief economist Stephen Koukoulas said.
Locally, there are current account data on Friday, with retail trade, building approvals and wages data as well as an RBA board meeting next week.

In the U.S., Alan Greenspan appears before a Senate Committee later today. There is also GDP data on Friday and the following week has the NAPM index and payrolls report, an FOMC meeting and the release of minutes from the December FOMC.
"This is a heavenly picture for traders and a scenario which could lead to watershed changes in market sentiment," he said.
On the data front, news of a 0.1 percent fall in December motor vehicle registations had no market impact.
The Treasury Corporation of Victoria made the first issue by a semi-government into the local market in 1997 on Thursday when it tendered A$100 million of its August 2008 stock.
Note: Canadian benchmark three year bond changed overnight, therfore no comparision made with previous spread.
Spreads closed narrower across the board and the futures curve continued its recent steepening trend, closing at its steepest in two weeks.
